newsitem.title: USA: Australia's Costello aims to privatize phone co.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello aims to privatize phone co.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday he expects the government to complete a planned selloff of one-third of its state-owned Telstra telephone company.
Speaking to reporters after addressing the Asia Society here, Costello also voiced optimism for plans to reform Australia's labor market.
"I'm pretty optimistic on both," Costello said.
"You never know in these sorts of situations until the vote is taken, but I think that there are good signs and good negotiations and good discussions going on," he added.

Costello also denied having received covert monetary policy insight from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, despite his comment that Greenspan saw no current threats to U.S. inflation after meeting the chairman on Monday.
Costello insisted he had not gotten "any inside views, nor am I giving out any views."
Though the remarks Monday triggered heavy buying of U.S. Treasuries and prompted calls for his resignation back in Sydney, Costello shrugged off reporters' queries about the maelstrom he created.
The whole affair is "not a controversy," he said.
